NINE-MONTH MEDIA PLAN

The Education × Business
Content Engine

A 9-month, funnel-led content system across blog, email, social and video, built to make us the authority for big schools and businesses: 1,000 target organisations, 10 corporate clients.

EDUCATE
ENGAGE
CONVERT
PUBLISHING RHYTHM: MONDAY + FRIDAY (EDU + BIZ)
PREPARED BY GRACE JUDE • 2026–2027
Reference principle adapted from the supplied strategy proposal.
2 / 36
01 — THE STRATEGIC IDEA

Stop treating social media as a posting schedule.

Build a repeatable content engine that moves high-value organisations from awareness ➔ trust ➔ action.

OLD MODEL

Post consistently
Hope for engagement
Count likes
Repeat (with no sales)

NEW MODEL

Identify audience problem
Provide highly useful content
Build proof & authority
Strong Call-To-Action (CTA)
Measurable Action

BUSINESS RESULT

Earned Attention
Conversations (DMs)
Qualified Enquiries / Leads
Corporate Clients & Partners
Core Principle: Every piece of content must have a job.
AUTHORITY CADENCE 1) Find what makes it hard • 2) Explain why • 3) Show the tool we built to make it simpler.
3 / 36
THE PHILOSOPHY

Fat Cow Strategy

Concentrate on the smallest levers that make the biggest impact.

CONCENTRATE
20% of the effort should generate 80% of the outcome (Good Strategy, Bad Strategy).
ONE FAT COW
One corporate client is like serving 50 regular customers, for far less effort.
THE TARGET
Identify 1,000 organisations. Win 10 corporate clients in nine months.
POSITIONING
Premium and selective. Word of mouth brings everyone else to our door.
RULE: We cannot serve everybody. Everyone will see the content, but we write it for the fat cows.
4 / 36
02 — OBJECTIVES

What the 9-month plan must achieve.

The strategy is designed around four specific outcomes.

1

AUTHORITY

Become the trusted, premium name among big school groups, institutions and businesses.

2

COMMUNITY

Create recurring interaction: questions, comments, saves, shares and conversations.

3

DEMAND

Win 10 corporate clients from 1,000 identified organisations; word of mouth brings the rest.

4

SYSTEM

Create a workflow the four-person team can repeat every week without chaos.

North-star question: “What should a viewer do next?”
5 / 36
03 — AUDIENCE

Aim at the few who matter, not “everyone”.

Content is written for about 1,000 high-value organisations. Everyone else sees it and refers us.

PRIMARY: THE FAT COWS

  • ✓ Large, established organisations with scale-level problems
  • ✓ Decision-makers who read their emails: no cold calls
  • ✓ Target: 1,000 identified organisations
  • ✓ Goal: 10 corporate clients in 9 months

EVERYONE ELSE: BY REFERRAL

  • • Parents, students, teachers and individual learners
  • • Small schools, SMEs and entrepreneurs
  • • They see the content and many will respect it
  • • We do not chase them; word of mouth brings them
Positioning: Like the iPhone: not made for everybody, yet respected by everybody.
6 / 36
FAT COW STRATEGY

Who are our fat cows?

Large, established organisations with scale-level problems: one list per product.

RESULTS PRO: EDUCATION

  • • School groups with 5–10+ branches across at least 3 states
  • • Government: ministries and agencies of education
  • • Funders and NGOs such as UNICEF and USAID
  • • Pitch idea: a quiz / competition platform

OFIA: BUSINESS

  • • Big, established logistics companies
  • • Major trade associations in the business hubs
  • • Multinationals not yet in Nigeria but doing well abroad
  • • Entrepreneurs wanting to break into Lagos (virtual office)
  • • Large real estate players and ERP / product-suite buyers
NOT OUR TARGET
Single-branch schools and small firms are too young and too small to pay. They come by referral.
7 / 36
THE TARGET ACCOUNT LIST

Build the list of 1,000

Know each one: who, where, what hurts.

01

NAME + ADDRESS

Organisation, head office, branches and states covered

02

CONTACTS

03

PAIN POINT

The likely problem at their scale, e.g. manual results across 10 branches

04

PRODUCT FIT

The product we have, or should build, to solve it

05

CONTENT ANGLE

The blog, video, graphic and email that speak to them

06

STATUS

04 — FUNNEL

One content engine. Three jobs.

The mix changes as the audience moves closer to action.

TOFU — AWARENESS
Reach the 1,000 target organisations • teach • surface their problems
MOFU — CONSIDERATION
Warm up the shortlist • show expertise • answer objections
BOFU — CONVERSION
Prove value • offer demos / design sprints • win the 10
Suggested Monthly Mix: 50% TOFU • 35% MOFU • 15% BOFU
10 / 36
FAT COW STRATEGY

Study them. Design for them. Sell to them.

The playbook behind every piece of content.

1

STUDY

Learn each organisation’s pain point and the product that solves it.

2

REACH

Content, email and LinkedIn. They read their emails, so no cold calls.

3

DEMO

Say yes to every demo. If it is not built yet, run a design sprint.

4

CUSTOMISE

Offer something tailored, e.g. a quiz engine for a ministry. Referrals follow.

Priority rule: Content for the fat cows comes first.
11 / 36
05 — CONTENT PILLARS

Six pillars keep the feed useful.

Varied and commercially relevant.

LEARN

How-to lessons, explainers, tips, frameworks

SOLVE

Problems, mistakes, myths, FAQs

PROVE

Case studies, results, testimonials, demonstrations

BUILD

Behind-the-scenes, people, process, culture

THINK

Opinions, trends, questions, industry conversations

ACT

Offers, invitations, lead magnets, consultations, next steps

06 — CHANNEL STRATEGY

Captions adapted to each channel.

One graphic + one video per idea, tailored for the audience.

LinkedIn
Decision-makers • target-account outreach • email follow-up • carousels
Instagram
Reels • carousels • community • visual education
Facebook
Parents • communities • longer captions • practical resources
TikTok
Fast education • hooks • demonstrations • discovery
WhatsApp
Nurture • direct response • reminders • offers
13 / 36
07 — PUBLISHING CADENCE

Two anchor days every week.

Monday and Friday, each with education + business.

ANCHOR DAY

MONDAY

PUBLISH

Education + business: graphic, video, blog and email from one idea each.

TUESDAY

RESEARCH

Research target accounts: pain points, contacts, FAQs, trends and objections.

WEDNESDAY

CREATE

Write blogs + emails, script videos, design graphics for Friday.

THURSDAY

QA & PREP

Edit, caption, thumbnail, fact-check, schedule and prepare replies.

ANCHOR DAY

FRIDAY

PUBLISH + DECIDE

Education + business again. Pick next week’s 4 ideas today.

SAT / SUN

PREPARE

Build Monday’s video + graphics. Review performance.

14 / 36
07 — FOUR FORMATS, ONE IDEA

Every main idea becomes four pieces.

The blog is the final destination. Everything points to it.

ONE CENTRAL IDEA

SOCIAL POST

Carousel or single graphic with a clear CTA.

VIDEO

Posted with the graphic; “Read more” leads to blog.

EMAIL

Directs readers to the blog with “Find out more”.

BLOG

Final destination: read more, engage, comment.

15 / 36
08 — THE 4-PERSON CONTENT BOARD

Clear ownership prevents delays.

No asset is “finished” until the next person can use it immediately.

CONTENT WRITER

Account research ➔ hooks ➔ scripts ➔ captions ➔ CTAs ➔ briefs

VIDEO EDITOR

Cuts ➔ subtitles ➔ pacing ➔ B-roll ➔ sound ➔ export formats

DESIGNER

Thumbnails ➔ carousels ➔ quote cards ➔ covers ➔ campaign assets

PUBLISHER

Calendar ➔ scheduling ➔ upload ➔ community ➔ analytics + account tracker

Three phases. Three different jobs.

18 / 36
11 — PHASE 1 (MONTHS 1–3)

Build trust and audience habit.

Goal: make the brand recognisable, useful and worth following.

MONTH 1
FOUNDATION
Theme: “Learn Something Useful”

Establish voice and format. Publish without expecting sales. Build the 1,000 target account list.

MONTH 2
PROBLEM / SOLUTION
Theme: “Why It’s Hard”

Highlight specific problems at the scale of 5+ branches. Connect them subtly to our tools.

MONTH 3
PROCESS / PROOF
Theme: “How We Build It”

Show the team, the code, the QA process and the logic behind the products.

19 / 36
12 — PHASE 2 (MONTHS 4–6)

Create demand.

Goal: move from “this is useful” to “this can help me”.

MONTH 4
PROOF
Theme: “Show Me”

Demonstrations, mini case studies, testimonials, before/after and process.

40% Proof • 35% Learn • 25% Act
MONTH 5
BUSINESS
Theme: “Learn ➔ Apply ➔ Grow”

Practical business education, productivity, career and money-making frameworks.

40% Learn • 35% Proof • 25% Act
MONTH 6
CONVERSATION
Theme: “Ask Us Anything”

FAQ series, response videos, live-style prompts, objections and community content.

35% Solve • 35% Proof • 30% Act
Primary KPIs: target accounts engaged • decision-maker DMs • enquiries • lead magnet downloads • demo requests
20 / 36
13 — PHASE 3 (MONTHS 7–9)

Convert and scale.

Goal: turn proven content themes into repeatable demand and partnerships.

MONTH 7
OFFERS
Theme: “Here’s How We Help”

Clear offers for named corporate accounts: who, outcomes, FAQs, objections and CTAs.

35% Proof • 30% Learn • 35% Act
MONTH 8
PARTNERSHIPS
Theme: “Let’s Build Together”

Collaborations, expert interviews, schools, businesses, community and referral content.

35% Proof • 30% Think • 35% Act
MONTH 9
SCALE
Theme: “What We’ve Learned”

Best-performing series, strongest lessons, proof, recap and next-stage campaign.

30% Learn • 30% Proof • 40% Act
Primary KPIs: demos / design sprints • corporate clients signed (goal: 10) • partnerships • referrals • content ROI

FRI Edu + biz: 4 formats MID / BOTTOM Prove + convert Read the blog

18 — DAY-TO-DAY OPERATING SYSTEM

What the team does between the two anchor posts.

The daily rhythm of production, publishing, and engagement.

MONDAY
Publish + Engage
Post 7–9am. Respond to early comments. Capture questions. Save strong comments for future videos.
TUESDAY
Research
Review analytics, target-account activity, FAQs and trends. Select next angles.
WEDNESDAY
Write + Design
Writer completes Friday script/caption. Designer creates thumbnail/carousel. Editor receives assets.
THURSDAY
Edit + QA
Editor finalises video. Publisher checks hook, subtitles, CTA, dimensions, spelling and brand consistency.
FRIDAY
Publish + Convert
Post 5–7pm. Team responds actively. Publisher logs views, watch time, comments, DMs and enquiries.
SATURDAY
Prepare
Build Monday’s video + graphics. Turn comments into prompts and next-week ideas.
SUNDAY
Review
15–30 minute review: winners, losers, lessons, next week priorities.

19 — CTA LIBRARY

Never end a post without a next step.

The blog is the ultimate destination.

TOP FUNNEL

  • → Read more on the blog
  • → Save this for later
  • → Share with someone who needs this
  • → Comment your answer
MIDDLE FUNNEL
  • → Tell us your biggest challenge
  • → DM “GUIDE”
  • → Ask your question
  • → Which option would you choose?
BOTTOM FUNNEL
  • → Book a demo
  • → Request a design sprint
  • → Book a consultation
  • → Send us a DM
  • → Start here
COMMUNITY
  • → Tag a friend
  • → Stitch / duet / respond
  • → Vote below
  • → Drop your question
  • → Tell us what to explain next

DEMO

RESPONSE

Turn a comment into the next post

EXPERT

Interview, quote, collaboration or guest

BEHIND SCENES

People, process, preparation and culture

OFFER

Who it is for ➔ value ➔ proof ➔ CTA

21 — HOOK LIBRARY

First 2–3 seconds: earn the next 10 seconds.

PROBLEM
“If you’re struggling with ___, stop doing this.”
CURIOSITY
“Most people get ___ wrong. Here’s why.”
RESULT
“Here’s a simple way to ___ in less time.”
CONTRAST
“You don’t need more information. You need this.”
LIST
“3 things every ___ should know before ___.”
QUESTION
“Would you know what to do if ___ happened today?”
MYTH
“No, ___ does not automatically mean ___.”
STORY
“We learned this the hard way…”

23 — KPI DASHBOARD

Measure the system at every stage.

AWARENESS

Reach among the 1,000 • views • unique viewers • follower quality

ATTENTION

3-second hold • average watch time • completion rate

ENGAGEMENT

Comments • saves • shares • replies • profile actions

DEMAND

Target accounts engaged • DMs • enquiries • demo requests

CONVERSION

Demos / design sprints • corporate clients signed (goal: 10) • partnerships

EFFICIENCY

Posts produced • turnaround time • top formats • content ROI

Rule: Do not compare raw numbers across platforms without considering audience size, format and objective.
32 / 36
24 — MONTHLY OPTIMIZATION

Every month: keep, improve, stop, test.

KEEP

Repeat formats and topics that consistently attract the right audience.

IMPROVE

Rewrite weak hooks, tighten editing, simplify CTAs and improve thumbnails.

STOP

Pause formats that repeatedly consume time without useful signals.

TEST

Run one controlled experiment: hook, length, format, posting time or CTA.

Monthly Management Meeting (45 mins)
Review dashboard ➔ identify patterns ➔ decide next month’s experiments.

26 — CONTENT GOVERNANCE

Quality control protects the brand.

  • ✓
    One post = one main message + one CTA, written for a named target segment.
  • ✓
    Facts, statistics, claims and testimonials must be checked before publishing.
  • ✓
    Never use a customer story or image without appropriate permission.
  • ✓
    Keep education practical; avoid jargon where a simple explanation works.
  • ✓
    Use the same naming, thumbnail and caption conventions across platforms.
  • ✓
    Every post gets an owner and deadline in the tracker.
  • ✓
    Archive final video, thumbnail, caption and performance data in one library.
"The goal is not perfection. It is consistent, trustworthy execution."
